items.followUp: Differentiate between an artery and a vein.

rubric.why: Identifies the thrombus as a clot that stays at its site of formation.
rubric.description: A thrombus is a blood clot formed in a blood vessel that remains at its place of formation.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as a clot and stating that it remains attached or at its place of formation.

rubric.why: Identifies the embolus as material that has detached and is moving in the circulation.
rubric.description: An embolus is a detached clot or other material that travels through the bloodstream.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is detached and travels through the bloodstream.

modelAnswer: A thrombus is a blood clot formed in a blood vessel that remains attached at its place of formation.
An embolus is a detached clot or other material that travels through the bloodstream.

items.followUp: Name the membrane enclosing the heart and state its function.

rubric.why: Locates the heart in the chest, between the lungs.
rubric.description: The heart is in the thoracic (chest) cavity between the lungs.
rubric.how: Award for locating the heart in the thoracic or chest cavity and between the lungs.

rubric.why: Gives the heart’s position relative to the body’s midline or nearby structures.
rubric.description: The heart lies slightly to the left of the midline; it is behind the sternum and above the diaphragm.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the heart is slightly left of the midline or giving another correct positional detail such as behind the sternum or above the diaphragm.

modelAnswer: The heart is located in the thoracic (chest) cavity between the lungs.
It lies slightly to the left of the midline, behind the sternum and above the diaphragm.
